subject: Cobalt Health — Latency degradation notice and coordination
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SEV-2: increased inference latency for Cobalt Health — initial sync

Team,

We’re seeing an elevated 95th/99th token latency starting ~08:45 PDT impacting a subset of Cobalt Health traffic (requests routed to eu-west-1 pool spilling into shared-hosted nodes). Error rate is still low, but tail latency is causing timeouts in their ingest pipeline.

Immediate asks:
- Ben: can you confirm whether any autoscaling misfires occurred in the eu-west-1 tenancy and share the node-level CPU/GPU utilization?
- Marissa: please stand up a customer line and prepare a short, non-technical blurb for Amelia.
- Evelyn: start capturing KV cache hit rates and prefix distribution; attach a latency snapshot to the runbook.

I’m opening INF-2987 and will join the bridge. Treat this as SEV-2 for now until we confirm impact boundary. I’ll post a customer-facing note within 30–45 minutes.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Park <amelia.park@cobalthealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 10:05:40 -0700
Subject: Cobalt Health — Service notice: elevated request latency (investigating)

Hi Amelia —

We’re writing to let you know we’ve detected increased inference latency affecting a portion of your traffic starting at ~08:45 PDT today. Our engineers have identified the event as a performance spike in the eu-west-1 serving pool which is increasing tail latency for long-context requests.

Impact: some requests may experience elevated latency or transient timeouts; we believe request correctness is unaffected.
What we’re doing: the ops team has opened INF-2987, is actively reallocating affected routes to a dedicated pool, and is capturing telemetry (latency snapshots, KV cache stats).
Mitigation ETA: engineers expect the reroute and mitigation to reduce tail latency within 30–60 minutes; we will confirm when metrics return to baseline.
Point of contact: Marissa Cole (marissa.cole@redwood.ai) is on the customer line and will provide live updates.
Next steps: we’ll follow up with a short post-incident note and a proposed postmortem with corrective actions no later than 72 hours.

We apologize for the disruption and will keep you updated with concrete progress.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Reliability, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0199

--

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 13:20:32 -0700
Subject: Cobalt Health — status update and next steps

Amelia / team —

Summary of current state: the reroute to dedicated capacity completed at ~12:50 PDT. Post-reroute telemetry shows 95th/99th token latency returning to baseline for 98% of affected requests; we’re continuing to monitor the remaining 2% which are longer-context requests. No data exposure or model correctness issues were observed.
What we did:
- Opened INF-2987 and initiated reroute to dedicated pool.
- Applied temporary config pin to prevent spillback to the shared pool.
- Captured latency_snapshot_20261005.csv and uploaded it to the runbook for your review.
Next steps:
- Engineering will run a targeted postmortem; we’ll share a one-page impact summary and action items within 72 hours.
- We propose a 30-minute review call tomorrow at 11:00 PDT to walk through root cause and mitigations; reply if that time doesn’t work.

We appreciate your patience — apologies for the disruption.

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
